title: Energy, Work and Power Module 2 Lesson 1: Energy Changes Single Body custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A particle of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ travels in a straight line with a speed of $14\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the kinetic energy of the particle.

A car of mass $1200\text{ kg}$ accelerates along a straight horizontal road from an initial speed of $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to a final speed of $22\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the increase in kinetic energy of the car.
A stone of mass $2.5\text{ kg}$ falls vertically downwards through a distance of $18\text{ m}$. Calculate the loss in gravitational potential energy of the stone. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A cyclist and bicycle of combined mass $75\text{ kg}$ travel $40\text{ m}$ up a road inclined at $8^\circ$ to the horizontal. Calculate the gain in gravitational potential energy. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A ball of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest from a height of $15\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground. Its speed immediately before hitting the ground is $16\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the work done against air resistance. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A hockey puck of mass $0.16\text{ kg}$ is hit with speed $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ across rough horizontal ice. The puck travels $36\text{ m}$ in a straight line before coming to rest. Calculate the magnitude of the constant frictional resistance force.

questions.prompt: A metal sphere of mass $1.5\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest from a platform $20\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground. The sphere strikes the ground with a speed of $18\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the loss in gravitational potential energy and the gain in kinetic energy of the sphere during the fall.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the work done against air resistance during the fall, and hence find the average magnitude of the air resistance force.

questions.prompt: A block of mass $5\text{ kg}$ is projected with speed $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ up a line of greatest slope of a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the initial kinetic energy of the block, and find the maximum vertical height the block reaches above its projection point before coming to instantaneous rest.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the distance the block travels along the plane before coming to instantaneous rest, and calculate the speed of the block when it has travelled halfway up this distance.

questions.prompt: A car of mass $900\text{ kg}$ travels up a straight hill inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta = 0.12$. The car accelerates from an initial speed of $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to a final speed of $18\text{ m s}^{-1}$ while travelling a distance of $150\text{ m}$ up the hill. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the increase in kinetic energy and the increase in gravitational potential energy of the car.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The driving force exerted by the car engine does $340000\text{ J}$ of work during this $150\text{ m}$ climb. Find the total work done against resistance to motion, and determine the average magnitude of the resistance force.

questions.prompt: A block of mass $6\text{ kg}$ is pushed up a line of greatest slope of a smooth plane inclined at $25^\circ$ to the horizontal by a constant pushing force $P$ acting parallel to the slope. The block passes through points $A$ and $B$ with speeds $14\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ respectively, where $A$ and $B$ are $20\text{ m}$ apart along the slope with $B$ higher than $A$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the decrease in kinetic energy and the increase in gravitational potential energy of the block as it moves from $A$ to $B$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By applying the work-energy principle, find the work done by the pushing force $P$ as the block moves from $A$ to $B$, and determine the magnitude of $P$.

questions.prompt: A skier of mass $70\text{ kg}$ descends a rough slope of length $80\text{ m}$ inclined at $22^\circ$ to the horizontal. The skier passes the top of the slope with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and reaches the bottom with speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the loss in gravitational potential energy and the gain in kinetic energy of the skier during the descent.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the work done against friction and air resistance during the descent, and find the average resistance force opposing motion.

questions.prompt: A particle of mass $4\text{ kg}$ is projected with speed $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the particle and the plane is $\mu = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}$. The particle travels a distance $d$ up the plane before coming to instantaneous rest at point $X$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the normal contact force on the particle, and express the work done against friction as the particle travels distance $d$ up the plane in terms of $d$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using the work-energy principle, calculate the distance $d$ to point $X$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: The particle then slides back down the plane from rest at $X$ to its starting point. Using an energy method, calculate the speed of the particle when it returns to its starting point.

questions.prompt: A parachutist of mass $85\text{ kg}$ drops from an aircraft at an altitude of $800\text{ m}$ above the landing zone. In Stage 1, the parachutist falls freely from rest through a vertical distance of $120\text{ m}$ before deploying the parachute, reaching a speed of $45\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at the end of this stage. In Stage 2, with the parachute open, the parachutist descends through the remaining $680\text{ m}$ and touches down with a safe landing speed of $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: For Stage 1, calculate the loss in gravitational potential energy, the gain in kinetic energy, and the work done against air resistance before the parachute opened.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For Stage 2, calculate the net change in kinetic energy, and calculate the total work done against air resistance by the open parachute and body during the descent to the ground.
